overview: A machine learning model by itself is just a file. An end-to-end system is a living machine that consumes data, trains models, monitors performance, and continuously improves.
In this module, we explore the 'MLOps' paradigm: building robust pipelines that take raw data from the world and turn it into reliable automated decisions.

topics.title: Data Pipelines & ETL
theory: Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) is the process of gathering raw data from various sources, cleaning it to meet model requirements, and storing it in a format ready for training.
Modern systems use tools like Apache Airflow or Prefect to automate these pipelines, ensuring that models are always trained on the freshest possible data.
visualIntuition: Imagine a water treatment plant. Raw water (dirty data) enters through pipes, goes through various filters (cleaning/transforming), and is finally stored in a clean tank (feature store) ready for the city to drink.
visualSuggestions: Pipeline diagram showing Data Source -> Cleaning -> Feature Store -> Training.
Comparison of manual data prep vs an automated 'DAG' (Directed Acyclic Graph).

code.content:
def extract(): return [" $100 ", "$200", "  50 "]
def transform(data): return [float(x.strip().replace('$', '')) for x in data]
def load(data): print(f"Data loaded to DB: {data}")

raw = extract()
cleaned = transform(raw)
load(cleaned)

topics.title: Model Training & Versioning
theory: In software, we version code. In ML, we must version code, data, and models. If a model's performance drops, you need to be able to 'roll back' to the exact data and parameters used for a previous version.
Tools like DVC (Data Version Control) and MLflow track experiments, allowing teams to compare hundreds of model runs and select the best one for deployment.
visualIntuition: Think of a laboratory notebook. Every time you run an experiment, you record the ingredients (data), the temperature (parameters), and the result (accuracy). This lets you repeat any successful experiment exactly.
visualSuggestions: Table comparing multiple model experiments (Experiment A vs B vs C).
Tree diagram showing model versions branching out from a common base.

code.content:
def log_experiment(params, metrics, version):
    print(f"--- Version {version} ---")
    print(f"Params: {params}")
    print(f"Accuracy: {metrics:.2%}")

log_experiment({'lr': 0.01}, 0.85, 'v1.0')
log_experiment({'lr': 0.001}, 0.92, 'v1.1')

topics.title: Monitoring & Concept Drift
theory: The world changes, and models eventually fail. 'Concept Drift' occurs when the relationship between inputs and outputs changes over time (e.g., shopping patterns change after a pandemic).
Continuous monitoring systems track the statistical properties of incoming data. If they detect a significant shift (Model Decay), they trigger an alert or an automatic retraining pipeline.
visualIntuition: Imagine a model trained to predict the price of a house. If the city's popularity suddenly skyrockets, the old prices become irrelevant. The model's 'intelligence' drifts away from reality like a boat drifting from a pier.
visualSuggestions: Time-series graph showing Model Accuracy slowly declining as 'Drift' increases.
Alert notification UI showing 'Statistical Anomaly Detected in Input Data'.

code.content:
def check_drift(old_mean, new_mean, threshold=0.1):
    diff = abs(old_mean - new_mean) / old_mean
    if diff > threshold:
        print(f"Warning: Drift detected! Shift = {diff:.1%}")
        return True
    return False

check_drift(100.0, 115.0) # 15% shift
